results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004952 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database. According to the database, the mushroom body is divided into these three parts: the calyx, which receives sensory interneuron afferents, the pedunculus, a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes, and the mushroom body lobe system, which consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch. Virtual Fly Brain holds extensive data related to the mushroom body, including neurons with some part in the mushroom body, neurons with synaptic terminals in the mushroom body, and images of neurons with some part in the mushroom body, among other types of data.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: The adult Drosophila brain contains several types of Kenyon cells, including alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells. According to the literature, these can be further subdivided into subtypes such as core, surface, posterior, anterior-posterior, middle, dorsal, and others, as stated in the VFB database, referencing Lee et al., 1999, and Aso et al., 2014. Specifically, the VFB database notes that there are three main subtypes that project their axons to the gamma lobe, the alpha and beta lobes, and the alpha' and beta' lobes. One of these types, the [gamma [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain")](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), is well-represented in VFB, with available data including images, subclasses, expression patterns, scRNAseq data, and transgene expression.

results.title: Neuroanatomy
results.question: What brain regions does the antennal lobe connect to?
results.response: The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") connects to the mushroom body and lateral horn. According to the VFB database, any antennal lobe projection neuron that sends synaptic output to the mushroom body, specifically the mushroom body calyx and lateral horn. This information comes from the VFB database, as summarized by the region connections query. Additionally, the [antennal lobe commissural pioneer interneuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe commissural pioneer interneuron in Virtual Fly Brain") may also play a role in these connections, but the specific details of its connections are not provided in the available evidence. results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response:
The [LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch0fva "Open LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") visual neuron type has the ID [1813403998](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch0fva "Open 1813403998 in Virtual Fly Brain"). It is a lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron, with a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer. The dendritic arbor extends outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer. LPLC2 is involved in detecting looming stimuli and is thought to play a role in eliciting a jump escape response. In terms of connections, LPLC2 has links to various neurons, including adult cholinergic neurons, T5c neurons, and transmedullary neurons. 

VFB holds information on 1813403998, specifically that it is a lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron. According to the literature, as summarized in VFB, this neuron type has a specific dendritic arrangement that allows it to detect looming stimuli, as described by Klapoetke et al., 2017, and Wu et al., 2016.

results.title: Anatomical containment chain
results.question: Trace the anatomical containment hierarchy from the DA1 glomerulus up to the top-level brain structure. What is each level in the hierarchy?
results.response:
The anatomical containment hierarchy from the [antennal lobe glomerulus DA1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003932 "Open antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 in Virtual Fly Brain") up to the top-level brain structure is as follows: antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 -> adult antennal lobe -> adult deutocerebrum -> adult cerebrum -> adult central brain -> adult brain. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database, which provides a detailed hierarchy of brain structures in Drosophila. 

According to the literature, the adult antennal lobe, which contains the antennal lobe glomerulus DA1, is part of the adult deutocerebrum, which in turn is part of the adult cerebrum (Grabe et al, 2016). The Virtual Fly Brain database further refines this hierarchy, indicating that the adult cerebrum is part of the adult central brain, and the adult central brain is part of the adult brain. 

VFB holds a range of data related to the antennal lobe glomerulus DA1, including neurons with some part in this glomerulus ([10](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") records), images of neurons with some part in this glomerulus ([911](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") records), and transgene expression data ([5](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") records).

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), also known as [DNp01](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open DNp01 in Virtual Fly Brain"), is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior (Thomas and Wyman, 1984). There is one of these cells per hemisphere (Koto et al., 1981; Namiki et al., 2018; Sturner et al., 2025) and its large cell body is located posterior to the lower protocerebrum (Koto et al., 1981). It can be identified by its large descending axon (Power, 1948), which is several times larger than any other axon in the cervical connective (Koto et al., 1981). The giant fiber neuron enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle (Ito et al., 2014) and descends on the ipsilateral side (Koto et al., 1981; Namiki et al., 2018), in the dorsal cervical fasciculus (Power, 1948). In the brain, it has dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center (Kamikouchi et al., 2009; Matsuo et al., 2016), where it receives substantial input from zone A and B Johnston organ neurons (Kim et al., 2020). It also arborizes in the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum and gorget (Matsuo et al., 2016; Namiki et al., 2018). 

The Virtual Fly Brain database holds information on the giant fiber neuron, including its anatomy and connectivity. VFB has [22](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") images of DNp01, [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") records of transgene expression in DNp01, [361](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") downstream connectivity classes, and [435](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") upstream connectivity classes. 

Relevant publications on the giant fiber neuron include Thomas and Wyman (1984), Koto et al. (1981), Namiki et al. (2018), Sturner et al. (2025), Power (1948), Ito et al. (2014), Kamikouchi et al. (2009), Matsuo et al. (2016), and Kim et al. (2020). 

Available driver lines for the giant fiber neuron are not explicitly mentioned in the provided information, but the Virtual Fly Brain database may hold relevant data on this topic.
